record.paper_title: PROGRESS IN THE OPEN PROBLEMS IN THEORY OF FUNCTIONS OF BOUNDED INDEX
record.original_question: Let L ∈ Q_b^n, let F be an entire function on C^n, and for r > 0 define G_r^b(F) as the union over zeros z of F of the discs {z + tb : |t| < r/L(z)} along the direction b. For z_0 ∈ C^n, let n_b(r/L(z_0), z_0, 1/F) count the zeros of the slice t ↦ F(z_0 + tb) in the disc |t| ≤ r/L(z_0), and let F(z_0 + tb) ≡ 0 force this quantity to be -1. Is F of bounded L-index in the direction b exactly when both of the following hold: (1) there exist r > 0 and P(r) > 0 such that for every z outside G_r^b(F), the logarithmic directional derivative satisfies |(1/F(z)) ∂F(z)/∂b| ≤ P(r)L(z); and (2) there exist r > 0 and n_e(r) ∈ Z_+ such that for every z_0 with F(z_0 + tb) not identically zero, and every t_0 ∈ C, one has n_b(r/L(z_0), z_0, 1/F) ≤ n_e(r)?

evidence.quote: We denote Gr(F) := G^b_r(F) = ∪_{z : F(z)=0} {z + tb: |t| < r/L(z)}, ... By n_{z0}(r, F) = n^b(r, z0, 1/F) := Σ_{|a^0_k|≤r} 1 we denote the counting function of the zeros ... If for a given z0 ∈ C^n and for all t ∈ C F(z0 + tb) ≡ 0, then we put n_{z0}(r) = −1. Denote n(r) = sup_{z∈C^n} n_z(r/L(z)).

Conjecture 2. Let F(z) be an entire in C^n function, L ∈ Q^n_b and C^n \ G^b_r(F) ≠ ∅. F(z) is a function of bounded L-index in the direction b ∈ C^n if and only if: 1) there exist r > 0, P = P(r) > 0 such that for each z ∈ C^n\G^b_r(F) inequality |(1/F(z)) ∂F(z)/∂b| ≤ P L(z) holds; 2) there exist r > 0, n_e(r) ∈ Z+ such that for every z0 ∈ C^n, for which F(z0 + tb) ≠ 0, and for all t0 ∈ C inequality n_b(r/L(z0), z0, 1/F) ≤ n_e(r) holds.
Note that Conjecture 2 from [10] is proved under the additional restriction 2n(r2)r1 < r2/λ_b(r2). It is currently unknown whether the condition is essential.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $b\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$ be a fixed direction and let $L:\mathbb{C}^n\to(0,\infty)$ be a continuous positive function belonging to the class $Q_b^n$, i.e. for every $r>0$,
$$\lambda_b(r):=\sup_{z\in\mathbb{C}^n}\sup_{|t_1|,|t_2|\le r/L(z)}\frac{L(z+t_1 b)}{L(z+t_2 b)}<\infty.$$
Let $F:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ be an entire function. Recall that $F$ is said to be of bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$ if there exists $m_0\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ such that for every $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and every $m\in\mathbb{Z}_+$,
$$\frac{|\partial_b^m F(z)|}{m!\,L(z)^m}\le \max_{0\le k\le m_0}\frac{|\partial_b^k F(z)|}{k!\,L(z)^k},$$
where $\partial_b F(z):=\sum_{j=1}^n b_j\partial F/\partial z_j$.

For $r>0$ define the exceptional set
$$G_r^b(F):=\bigcup_{z:\,F(z)=0}\bigl\{z+tb:\,|t|<r/L(z)\bigr\}.$$
For $z_0\in\mathbb{C}^n$, let $n_b(\rho,z_0,1/F)$ denote the number of zeros (counted with multiplicities) of the entire slice function $t\mapsto F(z_0+tb)$ in the disc $\{t\in\mathbb{C}:|t|\le\rho\}$ when this slice is not identically zero, and set $n_b(\rho,z_0,1/F):=-1$ if $F(z_0+tb)\equiv 0$ in $t$.

Assume $\mathbb{C}^n\setminus G_r^b(F)\ne\varnothing$. Decide whether the following equivalence holds:

$F$ is of bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$ if and only if both
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exist $r>0$ and $P(r)>0$ such that
$$\Bigl|\frac{\partial_b F(z)}{F(z)}\Bigr|\le P(r)\,L(z)\quad\text{for all }z\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus G_r^b(F),$$
\item there exist $r>0$ and $n_e(r)\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ such that for every $z_0\in\mathbb{C}^n$ for which $F(z_0+tb)\not\equiv 0$,
$$n_b\bigl(r/L(z_0),z_0,1/F\bigr)\le n_e(r).$$
\end{enumerate}
artifact.status_search_result: The equivalence is known to hold under the additional restriction $2n(r_2)r_1<r_2/\lambda_b(r_2)$, but whether this technical restriction can be removed appears to remain open. Subsequent works by Bandura and Skaskiv on directional logarithmic derivatives and zero distribution provide criteria of boundedness of $L$-index in direction, but a complete unrestricted proof of the stated equivalence has not been clearly established.

status_evidence.title: Directional Logarithmic Derivative and the Distribution of Zeros of an Entire Function of Bounded L-Index Along the Direction
status_evidence.snippet: New criteria of boundedness of the L-index along the direction are formulated in terms of restrictions on the distribution of zeros and the behavior of the directional logarithmic derivative.
status_evidence.claim: Partial criteria are established but a fully unrestricted equivalence is not stated.

status_evidence.title: Some criteria of boundedness of the L-index in direction for slice holomorphic functions of several complex variables
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient conditions for boundedness of L-index in direction via logarithmic derivative and zero distribution.
status_evidence.claim: Related criteria are obtained, indicating ongoing work toward the conjecture.
